sentences.text: Solicitor Daniel Okafor attended the meeting with client Rachel Penrose.
The purpose of the meeting was for Rachel Penrose to disclose information about her mother Margaret's financial and care situation, including concerns about her brother Martin's un
Margaret Penrose is 81 years old and has been diagnosed with dementia since two years ago.
Margaret Penrose lives at 81 Larch Road with carers.
Martin Penrose holds the power of attorney for financial and property matters for Margaret Penrose.
The power of attorney was signed by Margaret Penrose in 2023 and was registered.
Martin Penrose is the sole attorney; Rachel Penrose is not an attorney.
On 14 August, a transfer of £12,000 was made from Margaret Penrose's account to Martin Penrose's account.
The transfer was to an account in Martin Penrose's name, as indicated by the account numbers.
Rachel Penrose took photos of the bank statement on 14 August and printed them for reference.
On 22 September, Margaret Penrose told Rachel Penrose that Martin had made her sign a document without her understanding.
Margaret Penrose did not know what the document was or what it was for.
Rachel Penrose has not seen the document that Margaret signed on 22 September.
Brightwell care agency sent a letter dated 3 November stating that invoices are three months overdue and that they may stop calls if unpaid.
The outstanding care bills amount to approximately £2,400.
Martin Penrose has not said anything about selling the house, nor has it been put on the market.
Rachel Penrose has the letter from Brightwell dated 3 November.
Rachel Penrose has photos of the bank statement showing the £12,000 transfer on 14 August.
Rachel Penrose has not provided any document related to the document signed by her mother on 22 September.
Rachel Penrose wants to protect her mother's money and prevent Martin from accessing it.
Rachel Penrose is concerned that if Martin sells the house, there will be nothing left for her mother's care.
The solicitor advised that a transfer of £12,000 by an attorney without authority may be investigated by the Office of the Public Guardian.
The Office of the Public Guardian supervises attorneys and can request Martin to account for every penny of the transfer.
The Office of the Public Guardian can apply to the Court of Protection to cancel the power of attorney if necessary.
The solicitor advised that taking money as an attorney without proper authority may be a criminal offence.
The solicitor advised that an adult safeguarding referral to Wexley Council is appropriate due to Margaret Penrose being an adult at risk.
The solicitor advised that Rachel Penrose should not confront Martin about the financial matters at this time to avoid him moving money or becoming defensive.
Rachel Penrose will call Brightwell care agency tomorrow to explain that the bills are in hand and to prevent service interruption.
Rachel Penrose will email the solicitor the photos of the bank statement and the Brightwell letter by Friday, 27 November.
The solicitor will write to the Office of the Public Guardian by Tuesday, 1 December.
